content.text:
# BNG Controller — Add Alert Rule

## Objective
page when a BNG device's memory exceeds 90%

## Target namespace
`nok-bng`

## 1. PrometheusRule `spec` schema (live, from the cluster)
The following is the current `openAPIV3Schema.properties.spec` of the `prometheusrules.monitoring.coreos.com` CRD, read from the API server on every render. It is the source of truth for field names and types — do not rely on memory.

```json
{
  "description": "PrometheusRuleSpec contains the specification of desired alerting/recording rule groups. See https://github.com/prometheus-operator/prometheus-operator/blob/main/Documentation/api-reference/api.md#monitoring.coreos.com/v1.PrometheusRuleSpec",
  "properties": {
    "groups": {
      "description": "Content of Prometheus rule file. See https://prometheus.io/docs/prometheus/latest/configuration/alerting_rules/",
      "items": {
        "description": "RuleGroup is a list of sequentially evaluated recording and alerting rules.",
        "properties": {
          "interval": {
            "description": "Interval determines how often rules in this group are evaluated. Defaults to global.evaluation_interval.",
            "type": "string"
          },
          "limit": {
            "description": "Limit the number of alerts an alerting rule and series a recording rule can produce.",
            "type": "integer"
          },
          "name": {
            "description": "Name of the rule group.",
            "minLength": 1,
            "type": "string"
          },
          "partial_response_strategy": {
            "description": "PartialResponseStrategy is only used by ThanosRuler. See https://github.com/thanos-io/thanos/blob/main/docs/components/rule.md#partial-response",
            "pattern": "^(?i)(abort|warn)?$",
            "type": "string"
          },
          "query_offset": {
            "description": "Defines the offset the rule evaluation timestamp of this particular group by the specified duration into the past.",
            "type": "string"
          },
          "rules": {
            "description": "List of alerting and recording rules.",
            "items": {
              "description": "Rule describes an alerting or recording rule. See https://prometheus.io/docs/prometheus/latest/configuration/alerting_rules/ or https://prometheus.io/docs/prometheus/latest/configuration/recording_rules/#recording-rules for documentation.",
              "properties": {
                "alert": {
                  "description": "Name of the alert. Must be a valid label value.",
                  "type": "string"
                },
                "annotations": {
                  "additionalProperties": {
                    "type": "string"
                  },
                  "description": "Annotations to add to each alert. Only valid for alerting rules.",
                  "type": "object"
                },
                "expr": {
                  "anyOf": [
                    {
                      "type": "integer"
                    },
                    {
                      "type": "string"
                    }
                  ],
                  "description": "PromQL expression to evaluate.",
                  "x-kubernetes-int-or-string": true
                },
                "for": {
                  "description": "Alerts are considered firing once they have been returned for this long. Only valid for alerting rules.",
                  "pattern": "^(0|(([0-9]+)y)?(([0-9]+)w)?(([0-9]+)d)?(([0-9]+)h)?(([0-9]+)m)?(([0-9]+)s)?(([0-9]+)ms)?)$",
                  "type": "string"
                },
                "keep_firing_for": {
                  "description": "KeepFiringFor defines how long an alert will continue firing after the condition that triggered it has cleared.",
                  "pattern": "^(0|(([0-9]+)y)?(([0-9]+)w)?(([0-9]+)d)?(([0-9]+)h)?(([0-9]+)m)?(([0-9]+)s)?(([0-9]+)ms)?)$",
                  "type": "string"
                },
                "labels": {
                  "additionalProperties": {
                    "type": "string"
                  },
                  "description": "Labels to add or overwrite.",
                  "type": "object"
                },
                "record": {
                  "description": "Name of the time series to output to. Must be a valid metric name. Only valid for recording rules.",
                  "type": "string"
                }
              },
              "required": [
                "expr"
              ],
              "type": "object"
            },
            "type": "array"
          }
        },
        "required": [
          "name",
          "rules"
        ],
        "type": "object"
      },
      "type": "array"
    }
  },
  "type": "object"
}
```

## 2. Which Prometheus instances will evaluate this rule
- `nok-bng/bng-tel-prom`: requires labels `role=alert-rules`; namespace restricted to its own namespace (`nok-bng`) — the rule must live there; `evaluationInterval=30s`, `scrapeInterval=15s`.

**This is load-bearing, not decoration**: a rule created without the required labels, or outside an allowed namespace, is accepted by the API server and then silently never evaluated.

## 3. Metrics
Read `bng://metrics/available` before writing an `expr` — never invent a metric name; use only names it returns. Device metrics use the `source="<namespace>/<device>"` label convention (see `resolve_device_source` in `bng/common.py`); this label is not derivable from the metric name list.

For real, working PromQL against these exact metrics, read `bng://alerts/configured` — it lists the expressions of rules already deployed.

## 4. Further documentation
Links found in the current CRD schema:
- https://github.com/prometheus-operator/prometheus-operator/blob/main/Documentation/api-reference/api.md#monitoring.coreos.com/v1.PrometheusRuleSpec
- https://github.com/thanos-io/thanos/blob/main/docs/components/rule.md#partial-response
- https://prometheus.io/docs/prometheus/latest/configuration/alerting_rules/
- https://prometheus.io/docs/prometheus/latest/configuration/recording_rules/#recording-rules

For anything not covered above (PromQL function reference, alerting best practices, the `prometheus-operator` API reference), fetch it from the web if your client supports it — start from https://prometheus.io/docs/prometheus/latest/querying/basics/ and https://github.com/prometheus-operator/prometheus-operator. Clients without web access only have the schema, cheat sheet, and worked example in this prompt — say so rather than guessing PromQL syntax.

## 5. PromQL cheat sheet
| Category | Function | Description | Example |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Selectors | Exact match | Filter by exact label value | `up{job="x"}` |
| Selectors | Negative match | Exclude exact label value | `up{job!="x"}` |
| Selectors | Regex match | Filter by regex | `mem_bytes{pod=~"backend-.*"}` |
| Selectors | Negative regex | Exclude by regex | `requests_total{status!~"2.."}` |
| Time | Instant vector | Current value of a series | `metric_name` |
| Time | Range vector | Values over a window | `metric_name[5m]` |
| Time | Time shift | Shift eval time into the past | `metric_name offset 1h` |
| Rates | `rate()` | Per-sec avg rate (handles resets) | `rate(counter_total[5m])` |
| Rates | `irate()` | Per-sec rate, last 2 points | `irate(counter_total[5m])` |
| Rates | `increase()` | Total increase over a window | `increase(counter_total[1h])` |
| Aggregation | `sum()` | Sum over dimensions | `sum by (source) (metric_name)` |
| Aggregation | `count()` | Count active series | `count by (source) (up == 1)` |
| Aggregation | `topk()` | Top N elements by value | `topk(5, sum by (source) (m))` |
| Histograms | `histogram_quantile()` | Percentile from buckets | `histogram_quantile(.95, b[5m])` |
| Math | Error rate % | Ratio via binary operators | `rate(err[5m]) / rate(req[5m]) * 100` |
| Math | Utilisation % | Arithmetic between vectors | `allocated / total * 100` |
| Advanced | `predict_linear()` | Predict future values | `predict_linear(m[1h], 4 * 3600) < 0` |
| Advanced | `changes()` | Count value changes | `changes(process_start_time_seconds[1h])` |
| Advanced | Subqueries | Range query over a query | `quantile_over_time(0.99, m[1h:1m])` |

Patterns already used by this controller's own tools (`bng/tools.py`),
proven against these exact BNG metrics:

| Pattern | Form | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Label selector | `metric{source="ns/device"}` | The `source` convention — see §3 below |
| Gauge threshold | `state_..._cpu_usage > 80` | No `rate()` on a gauge |
| Counter rate | `rate(counter[2m])` | Window ≥ 4× `scrapeInterval` |
| Utilisation | `allocated / total * 100 > 90` | Guard `total` being 0 |
| Aggregation | `sum by (source) (...)` | Keep `source` to identify the device |
| Absence | `absent_over_time(metric[10m])` | Device-down idiom used in `bng/tools.py` |
| Label rewrite | `label_replace(...)` | Normalise `source` to `namespace/name` |
| Trend | `predict_linear(m[1h], 4*3600) > total` | Capacity-exhaustion forecasting |
| Combining | `and`, `or`, `unless` | Suppress an alert when another condition holds |
| Annotations | `{{ $labels.source }}`, `{{ $value }}` | Only valid in `labels`/`annotations` |


## 6. Authoring rules
- Set `alert`, never `record` — this tool only accepts alerting rules.
- Set `for` to at least twice the evaluation interval (eligible instance(s) evaluate every 30s — set `for` to at least double that).
- Add a `severity` label and `summary` / `description` annotations (annotation templating: `{{ $labels.source }}`, `{{ $value }}`, `{{ printf "%.1f" $value }}`, `{{ humanize $value }}`).
- Apply labels exactly as required by the selectors above — this tool does not add missing labels for you; a mismatch is reported back as a warning instead.

## 7. Worked example
```yaml
apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1
kind: PrometheusRule
metadata:
  name: system-resource-alerts
  namespace: nok-bng
  labels:
    role: alert-rules # Must match the ruleSelector above
spec:
  groups:
  - name: system-usage
    rules:
    - alert: HighCpuUsage
      expr: state_system_cpu_summary_usage_cpu_usage > 12
      for: 1m
      labels:
        severity: warning
      annotations:
        summary: "High CPU usage on {{ $labels.source }}"
        description: "CPU usage is at {{ $value }}% (threshold 12%)"

    - alert: HighMemoryUsage
      expr: (state_system_memory_pools_summary_total_in_use
        / state_system_memory_pools_summary_available_memory) * 100 > 2
      for: 1m
      labels:
        severity: warning
      annotations:
        summary: "High Memory usage on {{ $labels.source }}"
        description: "Memory utilization is at {{ $value }}% (threshold 2%)"
```

## 8. Next step
Once the manifest is ready, call `create_prometheus_alert_rule` with it as a single YAML or JSON string.
